paper_title: Integrating physics-based models with sensor data: An inverse modeling approach
combination_points: inverse modeling that fuses physics-based models with sensor observations
estimation of hidden or unmeasured state variables from partial measurements
physics-constrained data assimilation for multiscale inference
coupling local observables to macroscopic fluxes/rates through governing equations
combination_plan: Use an inverse-modeling/data-assimilation framework in which multiphase-interface physics models (mass, heat, charge, momentum, reaction transport) constrain and fuse heterogeneous modality-specific measurements, inferring unresolved nanoscale fields and connecting them to macroscopic evaporation, reaction, combustion, spray-drying, or cooling rates.
justification: The candidate’s core abstraction—integrating physics-based models with sensor data via inverse modeling—directly addresses the original problem’s bottleneck of partial, modality-specific observables by providing a principled way to infer coupled hidden states and link local interfacial heterogeneity to macroscopic transport and reaction outcomes.

paper_title: Acceleration of uncertainty updating in the description of transport processes in heterogeneous materials
combination_points: Accelerated uncertainty updating for transport processes
Probabilistic inference or Bayesian updating in heterogeneous media
Uncertainty propagation across scales in coupled transport models
combination_plan: Adapt accelerated uncertainty-updating methods from heterogeneous transport modeling to fuse multimodal interfacial measurements with physics-based transport models, enabling probabilistic inference of coupled nanoscale structure, chemical state, flow, temperature, and fluxes while propagating uncertainty to macroscopic evaporation, reaction, combustion, spray-drying, or cooling rates.
justification: Although the candidate paper is from a different domain, its focus on accelerating uncertainty updating in heterogeneous transport processes provides a transferable abstraction for the original problem: multiphase interfaces are heterogeneous, partially observed systems where local coupled transport variables must be inferred and connected to macroscale rates. Accelerated uncertainty updating can serve as a cross-domain mechanism for multimodal data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and scale bridging.

paper_title: Natural integration of scalar fluxes from complex terrain
combination_points: Conservative integration of heterogeneous scalar fluxes over complex boundaries
Upscaling/local-to-global flux aggregation using spatial weighting or footprint concepts
Coordinate or geometric mapping from irregular local sources to macroscopic flux budgets
combination_plan: Adapt the terrain-flux integration framework to multiphase interfaces by treating nanoscale structure, chemistry, heat/mass transfer, and flow measurements as spatially heterogeneous scalar flux contributions, then using conservative geometric/statistical upscaling to connect them to macroscopic evaporation, reaction, combustion, spray-drying, or cooling rates.
justification: Although the candidate concerns complex terrain rather than multiphase interfaces, its core abstraction—integrating spatially heterogeneous scalar fluxes across a complex surface into a coherent macroscopic budget—maps directly onto the problem of linking local interfacial heterogeneity to system-scale rates.
